Chief_Complaint.content: Upper lip swelling after prawn soup
Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC: Upper lip swelling after prawn soup

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Ate prawn soup at approximately 19:00 and upper lip swelling began about 30 minutes later, starting at the left upper lip corner and increasing.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Ate prawn soup ~19:00; swelling began ~30 min later; increasing; started at L upper lip corner

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports shortness of breath and is unsure about chest tightness.
Patient feels like her throat is closing and reports difficulty breathing.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Throat closing? Pt: “I feel like I can’t breathe that well right now.”

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Approximately one year ago the patient had a similar episode after late-night Chinese food, woke very swollen with difficult breathing.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Prior similar episode ~1 yr ago after late-night Chinese; woke very swollen; difficult breathing

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Initially the patient was alone at onset of current episode and her mother is now present.
Initially there were no antihistamines available, but the patient’s mother later found some.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: initially no antihistamines on hand, mother found some

Medications.content: Does not use a brown (preventer) inhaler.

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.content: Had a severe reaction to peanut as a child requiring hospitalization and an injection.
Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text: had severe reaction as child (hospitalized; recalls injection)

Assessment.content: Suspected anaphylaxis after prawn ingestion with acute progressive lip swelling, shortness of breath, and dizziness, onset within 30 minutes, with history of food-triggered reactions, peanut allergy, and asthma comorbidity.
Assessment.source_text: 1) Suspected anaphylaxis after prawn ingestion: acute progressive lip swelling, SOB, dizziness; onset within 30 min; hx food-triggered reactions; peanut allergy; asthma comorbidity

Assessment.content: Asthma managed with short-acting beta agonist only.
Peanut allergy with prior severe reaction.
Assessment.source_text: 3) Peanut allergy with prior severe reaction

Plan_of_Care.content: Call 999 for urgent emergency medical services due to suspected anaphylaxis and need for emergency department evaluation.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Call 999 for urgent EMS; suspected anaphylaxis → ED evaluation

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient to take available antihistamine while awaiting the ambulance.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Take available antihistamine while awaiting ambulance

Plan_of_Care.content: Ensure the patient is not left alone and that her mother remains present.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Ensure patient not left alone; mother to remain present

Plan_of_Care.content: After hospital care, arrange follow-up to obtain an adrenaline auto-injector and for allergy workup and education.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Post-hospital f/u to arrange AAI (epinephrine) and allergy workup/education

Follow_up_Information.content: Post-hospital follow-up planned to arrange an adrenaline auto-injector and allergy workup and education.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Post-hospital f/u to arrange AAI (epinephrine) and allergy workup/education
